previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old woman with a complex medical history including chronic diastolic heart failure, type II diabetes, chronic kidney disease, alcoholic cirrhosis, Crohn’s disease, and severe spinal stenosis was admitted after a mechanical fall during a funeral, with no loss of consciousness or head injury. She reported recurrent falls due to her legs giving out, attributed to spinal stenosis and chronic right knee pain status post replacement. Imaging showed bibasilar atelectasis but no rib fractures. Her kidney function was stable, heart failure was well-controlled, and diabetes managed with home insulin. Physical therapy recommended rehab, but the patient declined; instead, home physical therapy was arranged. She remained on her baseline medications with no additions or changes. She was discharged home with services, ambulatory with assistance, and clear instructions to monitor weight and follow up with her care team.
